nc_4_eastern_region.blurb: This is North Carolina's eastern climbing, mostly clustered in the Triangle around Raleigh, Durham and Chapel Hill. It is largely bouldering on small, local spots: boulders in city parks, beside creeks and along the Haw River, many holding only a handful of problems. Most are friendly, with plenty from V0 to V4 and a thin tail reaching toward V8. Roped climbing is a smaller part, with The Trestle the main sport and top-rope crag, mostly in the 5.8 to 5.10 range. Raleigh area climbing is the largest group, followed by The Trestle, the Carrboro and University Lake boulders and the Haw River Boulders. It suits quick sessions near town rather than a destination trip.

ri_arcadia_management_area.blurb: Arcadia is Rhode Island's largest management area, roughly 14,000 acres of woodland in the southwest of the state, crossed by logging roads and trails along the Wood River. The land was once farmed, and old stone walls and cellar holes remain in the forest. The climbing is almost all bouldering, scattered through the trees, with a little moderate top-roping. Problems run from easy to V10, with a good spread of moderates. Mt. Tom has the most problems by a wide margin, then Escoheag, with smaller groups at the Found Boulder, the Lost Boulder and Riverbed Boulder. Some of the boulders here are counted among the state's best.

sd_horsethief_lake_area.blurb: Horsethief Lake Area is part of the Needles in Custer State Park, in the Black Hills of southwestern South Dakota. The Needles are eroded granite pillars, towers and spires, and the climbing season there runs from spring to fall. Here trad climbing leads, with a good amount of bouldering and some sport routes. Roped grades run from about 5.6 up to 5.13, with the largest group around 5.10, and the boulders mostly span V1 to V9. The Chessmen is the biggest cluster of routes, followed by Horsethief Lake Bouldering and The Playground, with Primal Wall Area and Horsethief Spire adding smaller groups.

tn_middle_creek.blurb: Middle Creek is a bouldering area near Chattanooga, Tennessee, split into an Upper and a Lower section. The boulders are sandstone, and the climbing is all bouldering, with problems from V0 up to V10. The weight sits in the middle and upper grades, with the largest numbers between V5 and V7 and a steady supply of moderates beneath them. Upper Middle Creek holds roughly three quarters of the problems, spread over several small boulder groups, while Lower Middle Creek is the smaller section. Some boulders in the lower section stay wet through the summer months, so conditions vary with the season.

ut_gate_buttress.blurb: Gate Buttress is a crag cluster in Little Cottonwood Canyon, in the Central Wasatch of Utah, about a mile up the canyon. The rock is granite, described as world-class, and the canyon's rock overall is quartz monzonite. Trad climbing dominates, with a smaller share of sport and a few top-ropes. Grades run from easy fifth class through the 5.8 to 5.11 core to a few lines around 5.12. Schoolroom Area, East Gate Buttress and Beckey's Wall Area hold the most routes, with Dihedrals Area and Prune Face Slab next. The buttress holds the most popular crags in the canyon.

ca_auburn_sra.blurb: Auburn SRA lies in the Gold Country foothills near Auburn, in a network of rivers, canyons and dirt tracks with scattered boulders and small rocky walls. Climbing splits roughly evenly between bouldering and sport. Cave Valley, the old limestone quarry, is the main roped area, with highly featured limestone, and sport grades mostly in the 5.10 to 5.12 range. The Bar holds most of the boulders, with Tall Green Bridge and Mineral Bar Boulders adding more. Boulder problems run from easy to V8, concentrated in V2 to V6. Together they make a varied area with both rope and boulder days.
